{"id": "1c9ec64b-8f22-4976-8516-dc989e6cb20d", "role": "assistant", "content": [{"text": "I can't give you a status for this check, because I couldn't find any AWS-documented assessment that defines one. The check you describe looks like it comes from your own tooling or a third-party scanner. Its status vocabulary (PASS, FAIL, INCONCLUSIVE and so on) and the way it handles partial permission failures are defined by that tool, not by IAM or Bedrock.

What the evidence you described supports:

- **Roles:** the role check ran fully and found no role with AmazonBedrockFullAccess attached. That part is a clean pass.
- **Users:** the user check could not run, because `iam:ListAttachedUserPolicies` returned AccessDenied. You have no evidence about whether any user has the policy.
- **Overall result:** a plain PASS isn't justified, because users were never evaluated. A well-designed read-only assessment would report something like INCONCLUSIVE, PARTIAL, or ERROR/UNKNOWN. It would not report a clean PASS, and it would not report FAIL, since no violation was found.

Two other gaps could also hide the policy. The check doesn't cover groups (`ListAttachedGroupPolicies`). It also doesn't cover permission sets in IAM Identity Center. The policy could be attached through either of those.

To get a definitive answer, grant the assessment principal `iam:ListAttachedUserPolicies` (read-only). You could also run `iam:ListEntitiesForPolicy` on the AmazonBedrockFullAccess ARN. That one call lists every role, user and group with the policy attached. If you tell me which tool or runbook produces this check, I can look at its documented status semantics. I can also run the `ListEntitiesForPolicy` lookup against your account if you want.", "type": "text"}], "created_at": null}
